title: Psychological mechanisms of change in the interdisciplinary multimodal treatment of pain disorders of the musculoskeletal system – n-of-1.
summary: Pain is widespread in Europe, affecting many people physically, psychologically and socially. Musculoskeletal pain, such as chronic back pain, is particularly common. Multimodal treatment approaches have been shown to be beneficial, but not all patients benefit equally. Little is known about which treatment factors are effective for whom and why, and when changes occur during treatment. This study specifically examines changes in psychological variables and desired treatment outcomes during a 4-week, outpatient, interdisciplinary, multimodal group program. Pain intensity, psychological factors and physical activity will be recorded daily before, during and after treatment. It is expected that the psychological factors and outcome measures will improve during the intervention phase.
conditions: Diseases of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue

interventions.name: Intervention in the form of an interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy in an outpatient clinic. The treatment includes active treatment elements such as exercise therapy, relaxation techniques, physical therapy, manual medicine, psychotherapy and psychoeducation. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
People with chronic pain in the musculoskeletal system who require interdisciplinary multimodal pain therapy and have a hypermobility syndrome, previous outpatient treatment methods that have not been successful or have only been successful in the short term, written consent to participate in the study, sufficient knowledge of German and ability to understand and process the questionnaires and instruction material.
Exclusion criteria:
Participation in other studies, lack of group compatibility, inadequate physical capacity for the physical exercise program content, physical or mental illnesses that hinder therapy (e.g. significant internal illnesses or psychotic symptoms), clear conflict of interest between requesting a pension and alleviating symptoms, serious organic cause of pain (e.g. tumor, fracture, inflammation), pregnancy.
